counterexample_attempts: Reimplemented GF(2) polynomial arithmetic. All four Frobenius residues, three displayed Bézout congruences, and Rabin gcd checks recompute correctly.
Tested the Artin–Schreier exceptional case. A nonzero polynomial of positive odd degree cannot equal R^2+R over the algebraic closure because its pole at infinity has odd order.
Checked that the trace character is nontrivial despite Tr(1)=0; explicitly, Tr(alpha^29)=1.
Checked the endpoint d=1, where the character sum is zero, and d=65, where the certified maximum magnitude is 2^21.
Tried kernel and coefficient-cancellation cases. Evaluation at zero forces c=0, while any nonzero polynomial producing a zero word would contradict |S(P)|<=2^21<2^30.
Checked both signs of the Walsh sum and the cases P=0,c=0 and P=0,c=1. They give respectively the zero word and the all-one word.
Broke the generalized discussion lemma using m=2, D=3, K=F4, and a_3=1: Tr(x^3)=0 for every x, so a nonzero parameter tuple gives the zero word and the claimed dimension 5 exceeds length 4.
Checked the degree-67 boundary: its generic certificate is 535789568, exactly 32768 below the target.
Checked the Reed–Muller obstruction: RM(2,30) contains x_1x_2 of weight 2^28, far below the target.

line_audit.claim: The headline construction has length 2^30, dimension 991, and certified distance at least 535822336.
line_audit.justification: The independently checked field certificate, injectivity proof, and character-sum bound establish these parameters.

line_audit.claim: For every odd D<2^m, the generalized trace-polynomial code has dimension 1+m(D+1)/2.
line_audit.justification: The hypotheses do not ensure injectivity. For m=2,D=3 and a_3=1 over F4, Tr(x^3) is identically zero; moreover, the asserted dimension is 5 at length 4. The missing condition is (D-1)2^(m/2)<2^m.

line_audit.claim: The generic Artin–Schreier conductor certificate permits at most 33 full field-coefficient layers at the fixed bias budget.
line_audit.justification: For a reduced family, 2g equals total conductor degree minus 2. Requiring 2g<=64 forces conductor degree at most 66, hence at most 33 reduced odd principal-part layers. Adding the binary constant gives at most 33*30+1=991 dimensions within this method.

line_audit.claim: A degree-67 layer requires a nongeneric improvement to retain Walsh magnitude at most 64 sqrt(q).
line_audit.justification: The ordinary bound is 66*2^15=2162688, whereas the allowed magnitude is 64*2^15=2097152. The proposed extension is correctly presented as an open question, not a construction claim.

line_audit.claim: The distance audit covers every nonzero parameter case.
line_audit.justification: For P nonzero, its degree is odd and at most 65, giving |S(P)|<=2^21 and weight at least 535822336 for either c. For P=0, the only nonzero word is the all-one word.

line_audit.claim: The construction is deterministic and symbolically recoverable.
line_audit.justification: The modulus, polynomial basis, exponent set, coefficient spaces, evaluation set, coordinate order, and external binary constant are fixed. No sampling or length-changing operation occurs.

line_audit.claim: The object is a leaderboard candidate beating the dimension-31 baseline.
line_audit.justification: Its verified dimension is 991>31 at the exact required length and distance.

line_audit.claim: The cited additive-character theorem supplies |S(P)|<=(d-1)sqrt(q).
line_audit.justification: [Kowalski, Theorem 3.2](https://people.math.ethz.ch/~kowalski/exponential-sums-elementary.pdf) assumes a nontrivial additive character, d<q, and gcd(d,q)=1. Here the trace character is nontrivial, d<=65<2^30, and d is odd, so every hypothesis holds.

line_audit.claim: Rabin's criterion applies to the displayed degree-30 polynomial.
line_audit.justification: The criterion requires the n=30 Frobenius congruence and gcd checks at n/2=15, n/3=10, and n/5=6. These are precisely the checks supplied and independently recomputed. The cited [Rabin paper](https://doi.org/10.1137/0209024) is correctly identified.

line_audit.claim: The certified minimum-distance field is 535822336.
The listed next tasks distinguish verification and later publication work.
line_audit.justification: Materializing the embedded proof under proofs/ and adding a record are workflow steps, not missing hypotheses in the construction.

line_audit.claim: The degree-67 generic certificate misses the target by 32768.
The full quadratic Reed–Muller layer is inadmissible, while the stated six-layer subspace has dimension 211 and lies in C.
line_audit.justification: RM(2,30) contains x_1x_2 of weight 2^28. The six quadratic exponents 3,5,9,17,33,65, together with exponent 1 and the constant, form a subcode of dimension 1+7*30=211 by the proved injectivity.

line_audit.claim: All parameter-ledger values are correct.
line_audit.justification: The recomputed values are q=1073741824, 33 exponents, k=991, exact rate 991/2^30, Walsh bound 2097152, distance 535822336, relative distance 511/1024, and maximum exponent binary weight 6 at j=63.

line_audit.claim: The displayed Frobenius residues and Bézout congruences are correct.
line_audit.justification: Independent GF(2) arithmetic reproduced r_6, r_10, r_15, and r_30 exactly, and each displayed product has remainder 1 under its stated modulus.

line_audit.claim: T^30+T+1 is irreducible, so K has exactly 2^30 elements.
line_audit.justification: The verified residues satisfy Rabin's checks for all prime divisors 2,3,5 of 30, including T^(2^30)=T modulo p.

line_audit.claim: The evaluation image is a binary linear code of exact length 2^30.
line_audit.justification: K is a 30-dimensional F2-vector space; every one of its 2^30 elements appears exactly once in the specified coordinate order, and the parameter-to-word map is F2-linear.

line_audit.claim: Every nonzero permitted polynomial defines a geometrically nontrivial Artin–Schreier cover.
line_audit.justification: Its positive odd degree gives an odd-order pole at infinity, excluding an expression R^2+R over the algebraic closure. The affine curve is smooth because the derivative with respect to y is 1.

line_audit.claim: The cover has genus (d-1)/2, one rational point at infinity, and point count q+1+S(P).
line_audit.justification: Standard Artin–Schreier ramification at the unique odd pole gives different exponent d+1 and total ramification. Each affine fiber has two or zero rational points according to the trace, yielding the stated count.
line_audit.reference: algebraic-05.json:120, Character-sum lemma, ramification and point count

line_audit.claim: Hasse–Weil yields |S(P)|<=(d-1)sqrt(q).
line_audit.justification: The normalization is smooth, projective, and geometrically connected with genus (d-1)/2, so Hasse–Weil applies. The cited additive-character theorem independently gives the same conclusion.

line_audit.claim: The evaluation map is injective and dim(C)=991.
line_audit.justification: A kernel tuple has c=0 by evaluation at x=0. If its polynomial part were nonzero, the zero word would force S(P)=2^30, contradicting |S(P)|<=2^21. Distinct monomial degrees make P=0 equivalent to all coefficients being zero.

line_audit.claim: Every nonzero codeword has weight at least 535822336.
line_audit.justification: The weight identity handles both signs of S(P) and both values of c. The constant-only nonzero case has weight 2^30.

line_audit.claim: RM(1,30) is contained in C, and C is contained in RM(6,30).
line_audit.justification: Nondegeneracy of the finite-field trace pairing makes the exponent-one layer all linear Boolean functions. Each selected monomial has algebraic degree at most its exponent's binary weight, which is at most six.

line_audit.claim: The structured proof steps accurately summarize the dependency chain.
line_audit.justification: Field certification supports construction and the character bound; these give injectivity and distance. The RM containment is an ancillary consequence with no circular dependency.
